item.title: Trump Tried to Undermine the Nation’s Elections. It Didn’t Work.
item.description: Millions of Americans cast their ballots on Tuesday in an election that showed the resiliency of democracy. The president said he would accept the results.
item.dc:creator: Richard Fausset and Nick Corasaniti
item.media:description: A person wears a ‘Stop the Steal’ hat at a rally to support Ken Paxton, the defeated Republican nominee for Senate in Texas, at a rally in Lubbock last month.

item.title: The Many Meanings of James Talarico’s Winning Cowboy Boots

item.title: Nithya Raman Wins Los Angeles Mayoral Race, Defeating Karen Bass
item.description: The 45-year-old City Council member defeated the incumbent mayor, Karen Bass, 73, a sweeping success for a new generation of progressive leaders.

item.title: In Tight Mississippi Senate Race, Votes Are Carefully Scrutinized

item.media:description: Voting machines and ballot bags used in the midterm elections remain at the Hinds County Election Commission building in Jackson, Miss.

item.title: A Summit in China With Trump and Putin? That Might be Awkward for Xi.

item.title: Hegseth Lashes Out at Critics Calling for His Firing
item.description: In a new video, the defense secretary vowed to “finish what we have started.” Some Republicans say the Iran war was a big factor in their party’s midterm losses.
item.dc:creator: Greg Jaffe
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s defiant video is unlikely to quell calls for his impeachment or his dismissal.

item.title: Trump’s Triumphal Arch Wins Commission Approval Despite Court Challenges
item.description: President Trump’s 250-foot arch project was approved on Thursday by a federal planning board led by his allies. Court action and Democrats’ upcoming control of Congress could halt the plans.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater and Emily Badger
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:description: A model of President Trump’s proposed arch, seen in June.

item.title: Rubio Dismisses Reports He Will Leave His Jobs to Run for President
item.description: President Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser said he intended to stick with the administration to the end.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager and Anatoly Kurmanaev
item.media:description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said that he would support Vice President JD Vance if he ran for president.

item.title: Trump Moves to Make Oval Office a National Monument

item.title: 12 Planes in 12 Days: Pope Begins Major Latin America Tour, Weeks After Surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV’s tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru is his first major trip since an operation on his lung last month.
item.dc:creator: Motoko Rich
item.media:description: Pope Leo XIV offering Mass in St. Peter’s Basilica at the Vatican on Thursday.

item.title: Pope Leo’s Trip to Latin America: What to Know
item.description: Less than a month after lung surgery, Pope Leo XIV is landing in Uruguay on Friday, the first stop of a 12-day voyage across South America.
item.dc:creator: Motoko Rich, Emma Bubola and Julie Turkewitz
item.media:description: Pope Leo greeting a child in St. Peter’s Square at the Vatican on Wednesday. His trip to Latin America will be a test of his stamina.

item.title: Up in the Clouds With the Pope, It’s Still Commercial
item.description: Unlike American presidents, Pope Leo XIV has no private jet, so he travels on commercial airlines, like the rest of us. Well, almost.
item.dc:creator: Motoko Rich
item.media:description: Pope Leo XIV and Gennaro Anastasio, a senior cabin manager on many papal flights, after arriving in Turkey in 2025.

item.title: Stocks Erase Post-Midterm Elections Rally, Dragged Down by Tech
item.description: The S&P 500 slumped to its worst daily decline since April 2025 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq entered correction territory, as investors fretted about the durability of the A.I. build-out.
item.dc:creator: Joe Rennison

item.title: Newsom Commutes the Sentences of California’s 548 Death Row Inmates
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom, who is considering a run for president, called capital punishment morally objectionable. Though California hasn’t executed anyone for 20 years, that represents about a quarter of death sentences nationwide.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall
item.media:description: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California reduced every death sentence in the state to life in prison without parole, a sweeping move expected to face legal challenges.

item.title: DOJ Steps Up Leak Investigation on Supreme Court Decision Overturning Roe v. Wade
item.description: Investigators, using subpoenas and other law enforcement powers, are accelerating an inquiry that takes the Trump administration into the inner workings of the court.
item.dc:creator: Jodi Kantor and Michael S. Schmidt
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston for The New York Times
item.media:description: Protesters gathered at the Supreme Court in May 2022 after a draft of the decision to overturn Roe v. Wade was leaked.

item.title: Harmeet Dhillon, Leader of Justice Department’s Civil Rights Unit, Resigns
item.description: The move came after conflicts with Justice Department leaders, including disagreements over legal strategy in the midterm elections, people familiar with the matter said.

item.media:description: Harmeet Dhillon speaking to reporters in May.

item.title: National Guard to Expand Patrols in Washington With Military Vehicles and Boats
item.description: The Pentagon said that the decision by Pete Hegseth to widen the patrols was made on Oct. 29, just before a landslide defeat for Republicans in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: John Ismay and Chris Cameron
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: The National Guard deployment in Washington reached a high of 5,148 troops in July, as part of a surge of military forces ordered for the country’s 250th anniversary.
